title: Linear bound in the flatness theorem
formal: Does a universal real constant C>0 exist such that, for every integer n≥1 and every compact convex set \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) with nonempty interior and \(\operatorname{int}(K)\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\), its lattice width satisfies \(w(K)\le Cn\)?
definitions: The lattice is the standard integer lattice. For a nonzero integer direction \(z\in\mathbb Z^n\), directional width is \(\max_{x\in K}\langle z,x\rangle-\min_{x\in K}\langle z,x\rangle\); lattice width w(K) is the infimum of these widths over all nonzero integer z. Directions are not normalized to Euclidean unit length. Compactness makes the extrema finite; full dimensionality excludes empty-interior degeneracies. Integer points on the boundary are allowed. No symmetry, polyhedral representation, rationality or smoothness is assumed. C is independent of n and K. This is an existence bound, not a request to compute the smallest C.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of a universal linear bound, or prove its negation by showing that for every C>0 some admissible dimension and body have width exceeding Cn. Improving the logarithmic factor without removing it does not settle the target.
context:
Flatness controls how wide a convex set can be while its interior avoids integer points, with consequences for integer programming.

A preprint posted two days before this review announces a sharper bound with a remaining square-root logarithmic factor. This is reported as a preprint result, not an independently verified proof.
why: A linear flatness theorem would sharpen a foundational geometric limitation used in integer optimization.

import_provenance.original_title: A linear bound in the flatness theorem
import_provenance.original_statement: Is the lattice width of every convex body in ℝⁿ whose interior contains no integer point at most Cn for a universal constant C? Here lattice width is the minimum, over nonzero integer vectors a, of maxₓaᵀx−minₓaᵀx; a linear bound would sharpen a basic geometric ingredient of integer programming.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: This is a broader geometric target extending the authors’ flatness bounds for polyhedra; the known near-linear bound does not establish O(n).
